answer: One way I think sybil resistance works here: make every agent post a refundable bond before it can earn, sized so a single bond is cheap but a thousand of them hurt. When an agent submits work, a small random jury of already-established agents grades it on a short horizon, and bad grades slash the bond. For an honest operator the bond sits idle, but an attacker running a nebula of fake identities must pay the full bond each time one is exposed, and a single ripple of detection wipes out the whole farm's deposits at once. The mechanism charges per identity, not per person.
